entries.name: .NET MAUI
entries.use_for: Cross-platform native apps for Android, iOS, macOS and Windows in C#
entries.why: Microsoft official successor to Xamarin.Forms; the default for .NET teams building mobile apps.
entries.summary: Microsoft's .NET Multi-platform App UI: a C# and XAML framework to build native apps for Android, iOS, iPadOS, macOS and Windows from a single codebase.
entries.best_for: C#/.NET teams building cross-platform mobile and desktop apps with shared code.
entries.not_for: Tied to the .NET ecosystem; no Linux desktop target, and web developers are better served by React Native or Capacitor.

entries.name: Capacitor
entries.use_for: Ship an existing web app as a native iOS/Android app with access to native APIs.
entries.why: Modern successor to Cordova; works with any web framework and keeps native projects editable.
entries.summary: Cross-platform native runtime that wraps a web app as an iOS or Android app, with a plugin API for native SDKs and first-class PWA support.
entries.best_for: Shipping an existing web app (any framework) to app stores with access to native APIs.
entries.not_for: The UI runs in a WebView, so not truly native rendering; heavy animation or complex native UI may suffer.

entries.name: Compose Multiplatform
entries.use_for: Share Kotlin UI code across Android, iOS, desktop and web with Jetpack Compose.
entries.why: JetBrains framework that extends Jetpack Compose to iOS, letting Kotlin teams share UI and logic.
entries.summary: Declarative Kotlin UI framework based on Jetpack Compose for sharing UI code across Android, iOS, desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) and web (beta).
entries.best_for: Kotlin teams sharing UI between Android, iOS and desktop.
entries.not_for: Requires Kotlin; web target is beta and the iOS ecosystem is less mature than Flutter or React Native.

entries.name: Detox
entries.use_for: Gray-box end-to-end testing for React Native apps
entries.why: Synchronises with the app runtime to avoid flaky waits; the standard E2E tool for RN on simulators and devices.
entries.summary: Gray-box end-to-end testing and automation framework for mobile apps, mainly React Native, running tests on simulators and devices and synchronizing with the app.
entries.best_for: E2E testing of React Native apps in CI with reduced flakiness.
entries.not_for: Aimed at React Native; setup is involved, and it is not a unit-testing tool.

entries.name: Expo
entries.use_for: Build, run and ship React Native apps with managed native modules, routing and cloud builds.
entries.why: Recommended way to start React Native apps; Expo Router, EAS Build and OTA updates remove most native setup.
entries.summary: Open-source platform for universal React Native apps: Expo SDK and Modules API, Router, CLI and Expo Go, with EAS cloud services for builds and updates.
entries.best_for: Starting or scaling React Native apps with managed native modules, file-based routing and cloud builds.
entries.not_for: EAS hosted services have paid tiers; apps with unusual native needs may need prebuild or custom dev clients.

entries.name: fastlane
entries.use_for: Automate iOS/Android builds, signing, screenshots and store releases
entries.why: The standard mobile release automation tool, used across native, Flutter and React Native apps.
entries.summary: Ruby tool automating iOS and Android tasks: building, code signing and provisioning profiles, screenshots and store releases, scripted via Fastfiles.
entries.best_for: Automating repeatable mobile build, signing and store-release pipelines in CI.
entries.not_for: Ruby-based and requires Apple/Google credentials; not a build system itself.

entries.name: FlashList
entries.use_for: Fast, recycling list component for React Native, a drop-in FlatList replacement
entries.why: Shopify-built; dramatically smoother long lists, widely recommended for Expo apps.
entries.summary: High-performance list component for React Native that recycles cells; v2 is a JS-only rewrite for the new architecture and a drop-in FlatList replacement.
entries.best_for: Long or complex React Native lists where FlatList shows blank cells or stutters.
entries.not_for: v2 targets the new architecture; overkill for short lists.

entries.name: Flutter
entries.use_for: Build natively compiled mobile (and web/desktop) apps from one Dart codebase.
entries.why: Google-backed, own rendering engine for pixel-consistent UI and fast hot reload; very large package ecosystem.
entries.summary: Google's UI toolkit for building natively compiled apps for mobile, web and desktop from a single Dart codebase, with its own rendering engine.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting one codebase with consistent custom UI across iOS, Android, web and desktop.
entries.not_for: Requires Dart; own renderer means non-native widgets and larger app size, and web is weaker for SEO-heavy sites.

entries.name: Gifted Chat
entries.use_for: Complete chat UI for React Native apps
entries.why: Drop-in chat screen with bubbles, input toolbar, avatars and load-earlier; saves weeks of messaging UI.
entries.summary: Chat UI component set for React Native and web with customizable components, composer and message rendering. The README says it is now in maintenance mode, with development moved to a fork.
entries.best_for: Quickly adding a chat interface to a React Native app (existing projects).
entries.not_for: In maintenance mode with no new features; the README points new projects to the @kesha-antonov/react-native-chat fork. UI only, no backend.

entries.name: Ionic Framework
entries.use_for: Build mobile-styled UIs for hybrid apps and PWAs with React, Vue or Angular.
entries.why: Mature mobile UI toolkit with platform-adaptive iOS/Android styling, usually paired with Capacitor.
entries.summary: Web-component-based UI toolkit with mobile-styled components for building hybrid mobile apps and PWAs with Angular, React or Vue, typically packaged with Capacitor.
entries.best_for: Web teams building mobile-styled hybrid apps or PWAs from one JS codebase.
entries.not_for: Hybrid WebView rendering rather than native widgets; not for apps needing platform-native UI.

entries.name: Lynx
entries.use_for: Write native mobile UIs with web-style markup, CSS and ReactLynx
entries.why: ByteDance open-sourced engine behind TikTok features; dual-threaded native rendering for web developers.
entries.summary: ByteDance's family of technologies for writing native mobile and web UIs with web-style markup and CSS, including ReactLynx, rendered natively on Android, iOS and web.
entries.best_for: Web developers wanting native rendering from CSS and React-style code.
entries.not_for: Younger ecosystem with fewer libraries and community answers than React Native or Flutter.

entries.name: NativeScript
entries.use_for: Build native iOS/Android apps in TypeScript with direct native API access
entries.why: OpenJS project; lets JS/Angular/Vue/Svelte devs call platform APIs directly without bridges.
entries.summary: Framework that exposes native iOS, Android and visionOS APIs directly to JavaScript/TypeScript runtimes for building native apps, with CLI and framework flavors.
entries.best_for: Developers wanting direct access to native platform APIs from JS/TS without writing bridges.
entries.not_for: Smaller community than React Native or Flutter; fewer ready-made third-party plugins.

entries.name: NativeWind
entries.use_for: Use Tailwind CSS classes to style React Native components
entries.why: The standard way to bring Tailwind to React Native/Expo; base of React Native Reusables.
entries.summary: Styling library bringing Tailwind CSS classes to React Native, choosing the right style engine per platform; it is not a component library.
entries.best_for: React Native or Expo projects where the team already uses Tailwind.
entries.not_for: Provides styling only; you still need components, and the Tailwind-to-native mapping has limitations.

entries.name: React Native
entries.use_for: Build native iOS and Android apps with React and JavaScript/TypeScript.
entries.why: The most used JS mobile framework, backed by Meta with the New Architecture and a large library ecosystem.
entries.summary: Framework for building native Android and iOS apps with React; JavaScript components render to native platform UI views.
entries.best_for: Teams with React skills building native mobile apps with shared logic.
entries.not_for: Needs native tooling and occasional native code; Expo is the usual recommended starting point.

entries.name: React Native Calendars
entries.use_for: Calendar, agenda and date-marking components for React Native
entries.why: Pure-JS, customizable calendar and agenda views used widely for booking and scheduling screens.
entries.summary: Pure-JS calendar, agenda and date-marking components for React Native with dot, multi-dot and period marking, swipeable calendars, customization and locale support.
entries.best_for: Adding calendars, agendas and date range selection to a React Native app.
entries.not_for: Not a scheduling or full event-calendar system; UI components only.

entries.name: React Native Elements
entries.use_for: Cross-platform UI toolkit for React Native
entries.why: Long-standing, themeable RN component kit (buttons, inputs, lists, cards).
entries.summary: Cross-platform React Native UI toolkit of customizable components such as buttons, inputs and lists, split into packages (@rneui/base, @rneui/themed).
entries.best_for: Quickly assembling standard React Native screens with themeable components.
entries.not_for: Less actively favored than newer kits; not Material Design-specific and not a design system in itself.

entries.name: React Native Firebase
entries.use_for: Native Firebase SDK bindings for React Native
entries.why: Modular, well-tested wrappers for Auth, Firestore, Messaging, Crashlytics and more on iOS and Android.
entries.summary: React Native modules connecting to native Firebase SDKs on iOS and Android as a thin JS layer, covering auth, Firestore, messaging, analytics and more.
entries.best_for: React Native apps using Firebase services natively, including push notifications.
entries.not_for: Needs native setup, so no Expo Go (dev builds required); tied to Firebase.

entries.name: React Native for Web
entries.use_for: Run React Native components and APIs in the browser to share code with web.
entries.why: Mature compatibility layer used by Expo for web and by large production web apps.
entries.summary: Compatibility layer that runs React Native components and APIs in the browser, built on react-dom, to share code between native and web.
entries.best_for: Sharing UI code between React Native apps and web (used by Expo web and Tamagui).
entries.not_for: Web output is not a full web-idiomatic design; some native-only APIs are unsupported.

entries.name: React Native Gesture Handler
entries.use_for: Native-driven touch and gesture system for React Native
entries.why: Core dependency of React Navigation and most RN apps; gestures run on the UI thread.
entries.summary: Declarative API exposing the platform's native touch and gesture system to React Native, running gestures natively for smooth and reliable interactions.
entries.best_for: Complex gestures (pan, pinch, swipe) in React Native, often with Reanimated.
entries.not_for: Requires native install and setup; unnecessary for simple tap-only interfaces.

entries.name: React Native Navigation
entries.use_for: Fully native navigation for React Native
entries.why: Wix library using real native navigation stacks and tabs instead of JS-driven ones.
entries.summary: Navigation library for React Native providing fully native navigation on iOS and Android with a cross-platform JS API.
entries.best_for: Apps that want truly native navigation stacks and tabs.
entries.not_for: Native integration is more complex; most new projects use React Navigation or Expo Router, and Expo support is limited.

entries.name: React Native Paper
entries.use_for: Material Design component library for React Native
entries.why: Callstack-maintained, themeable Material 3 components with good accessibility.
entries.summary: Material Design component library for React Native with themeable, production-ready components that follow Material specs on both platforms.
entries.best_for: Apps wanting a Material Design look with theming and dark mode.
entries.not_for: Material styling by default; a less natural fit for iOS-native look or heavy brand customization.

entries.name: React Native Reusables
entries.use_for: Copy shadcn/ui-style components into a React Native app styled with NativeWind.
entries.why: Brings the shadcn copy-paste model and look to React Native, built on accessible primitives.
entries.summary: shadcn/ui-style, copy-paste component collection for React Native styled with NativeWind, so you own the component code.
entries.best_for: Expo/React Native projects using NativeWind that want shadcn-style components.
entries.not_for: Depends on NativeWind; not a packaged npm component library, and README documentation is thin.

entries.name: React Native Vector Icons
entries.use_for: Use popular icon sets (Material, FontAwesome, Ionicons) in React Native apps.
entries.why: The most used icon package for React Native, with many bundled icon sets.
entries.summary: Vector icon sets (Material, FontAwesome, Ionicons and more) for React Native, usable in buttons, tab bars and navigation, now split into per-set packages.
entries.best_for: Adding standard icon fonts to React Native UIs.
entries.not_for: Font-based icons; for native SVG use a different package, and bundling many sets adds size.

entries.name: React Navigation
entries.use_for: Add stack, tab and drawer navigation to a React Native app.
entries.why: The standard navigation library for React Native and the base Expo Router builds on.

license_verified.note: MIT license files live in each package folder (e.g. packages/native/LICENSE).

entries.summary: Routing and navigation library for React Native with stack, tab and drawer navigators; this branch is v8, with 7.x being the latest stable.
entries.best_for: Standard in-app navigation for React Native apps (JS-based, widely used).
entries.not_for: Navigation is JS-driven, not native stacks; this branch is a pre-release major version.

entries.name: react-native-maps
entries.use_for: Native map views for React Native on iOS and Android
entries.why: The standard RN map component with markers, polygons and overlays on Google and Apple Maps.
entries.summary: Native map components (Apple Maps and Google Maps) for React Native on iOS and Android, with markers, polygons and overlays declared as children of MapView.
entries.best_for: Showing maps with markers and shapes in React Native apps.
entries.not_for: Mobile only; Google Maps needs API keys, and web support is not part of it.

entries.name: Reactotron
entries.use_for: Inspect state, network calls and logs of React Native apps while developing.
entries.why: Long-standing desktop debugger for RN with Redux/MobX-State-Tree plugins, maintained by Infinite Red.
entries.summary: Desktop debugging app for React and React Native that shows state, network requests, logs and performance metrics from your running app.
entries.best_for: Inspecting state, API calls and logs while developing React Native apps.
entries.not_for: A development tool only, not production monitoring; some features need the app configured with the client.

entries.name: Tamagui
entries.use_for: Universal UI kit and optimizing style compiler for React Native and web
entries.why: Share styled components across Expo and Next.js with compile-time optimization.
entries.summary: Universal style library, UI kit and optimizing compiler for React and React Native that extracts styles at build time for web and native sharing.
entries.best_for: Sharing UI and design system between web and native with strong performance.
entries.not_for: Complex configuration and compiler setup; steeper learning curve than simpler style libraries.

entries.name: Taro
entries.use_for: Write once in React/Vue, ship to WeChat/Alipay mini programs, H5 and React Native
entries.why: The leading framework for Chinese mini-program platforms with React Native and web targets.
entries.summary: Taro is a cross-platform framework for writing one codebase in React, Vue or Nerv and running it as WeChat, JD, Baidu, Alipay, ByteDance or QQ mini-programs, H5 web, or React Native apps. It has a UI library ecosystem such as taro-ui and NutUI.
entries.best_for: Teams targeting Chinese mini-program platforms (WeChat and others) plus web and React Native from a single React or Vue codebase.
entries.not_for: Apps that do not target mini-programs, where plain React Native or Flutter may fit better. Docs and community are mostly Chinese, and Taro 1/2 projects need migration to Taro 3.

entries.name: UI Kitten
entries.use_for: Themeable React Native UI library on Eva Design System
entries.why: 30+ accessible components with runtime theme switching driven by design tokens.
entries.summary: Themeable React Native UI library on the Eva Design System with 30+ components, light and dark themes and runtime theme switching; v6 supports React 19.
entries.best_for: Apps wanting a themeable component set with Eva design and runtime theme changes.
entries.not_for: Smaller community than Paper or Tamagui; v5 to v6 requires migration.

entries.name: VisionCamera
entries.use_for: High-performance camera library for React Native with frame processors
entries.why: The standard RN camera library: photo, video, QR scanning and real-time ML frame processing.
entries.summary: High-performance React Native camera library for photo and video capture, QR/barcode scanning, multi-camera, and frame processors (JS worklets) for ML and shaders.
entries.best_for: Camera features, barcode scanning or real-time frame processing (face detection, AI) in React Native.
entries.not_for: Requires native setup and dev builds (no Expo Go); frame processors need Reanimated worklets.

entries.name: WatermelonDB
entries.use_for: Reactive offline-first database for React Native
entries.why: Lazy-loaded SQLite-backed DB that stays fast with tens of thousands of records, with a sync protocol.
entries.summary: Reactive, lazy-loading, offline-first database for React and React Native that scales to tens of thousands of records and syncs with your own backend.
entries.best_for: Data-heavy React Native apps needing fast launch, observables and offline sync.
entries.not_for: You must implement sync endpoints on your own backend; heavier than AsyncStorage or SQLite wrappers for small apps.
